detailed_review.score_reasoning: Baseline 7. The page started at 10 and lost 2.5 across three findings: F1 at 1, a self-contradiction about where a product reader stops reading, which on the wiki's only navigation surface sent that reader through five contributor pages; F2 at 1, a coverage clause that routed an update-seeking reader to the page saying updating is not built while the working by-hand procedure sat on a page the same sentence described as something else; and F3 at 0.5, a last_reviewed date one day behind the edits it covers. 10 - 2.5 = 7.5, floored to 7, which is NEEDS_WORK. After: all three are in changed[] and remaining[] is empty, so open_penalty is 0 and the arithmetic gives 10. The cap in the scoring rules applies because further_improvements is non-empty, so score_after is 9 and the delta is +2. Nothing about the type was wrong at any point: Pass 0 found no wrong-type, type-mixture or missing-spine, because the declared type: landing matches what all six sections do, and every derived objective sits at Remember or Understand, which is the level a landing page should carry.
detailed_review.what_worked: F2 is the one that mattered most to a reader with a keyboard in front of them. The index is the only navigation surface the published wiki has, and its ## Getting started prose told a reader that updating in place is not built yet, full stop. That is true of the design and false of the reader's actual question, because wiki/installing.md:247-259 carries two numbered steps that get a new build onto a machine today. The clause now separates the two: what the install does and how you update by hand, then the unbuilt design for updating in place. The three clauses still map one to one onto the three links in link order, which is the property the author restored when the macOS link came out, so the fix did not cost the correspondence it had just gained. F1 removed a contradiction the page was making with itself. It said a reader who came to use Hearth could stop above ## Looking under the hood, while the section directly above opened by saying it is for a reader who cloned the repository. The stopping point now names the real boundary and marks both section names as section names, so the sentence cannot be misread as the act of running Hearth on a device. F3 is small and it is the kind of thing that rots quietly: the freshness date now matches the day the page changed. Separately, the delivered change itself checks out against source rather than against the author's report. The macOS install link is gone, meeting-your-persona.md is first in its section, and a hand enumeration of the 29 published pages against the 26 index targets confirms all 26 are distinct and that the only page with no index entry is the ratified transient orphan.
detailed_review.what_holds_score_down: Nothing is open as a finding: remaining[] is empty and open_penalty is 0. The score is 9 rather than 10 because the improvements below are real and naming them honestly is worth more than the tenth point. Two of them are handoffs already recorded as checklist entries C1 and C2, both deferred to the orchestrator. The one that touches a reader directly is the transient orphan: wiki/install-macos.md still publishes and now has no index entry and no rail entry, so between this task and T16 it is a page in the corpus that the corpus cannot reach. That is the ratified design and it is recorded as an objective gap rather than a defect, but it is a gap while it lasts. The rest are pressure rather than damage. Three of the six section paragraphs now run between 49 and 58 words against a 60-word limit, so the next editor to add a clause anywhere in this page will trip a long-paragraph warning rather than have room to work. And the hardware floor at :24-26 is a product fact living on a page whose type says it should carry almost no detail of its own, which makes it a second place for the 8 GB figure to go stale.
